compounds.name: Pre-Monsoon Sun & Heat
compounds.mechanism: Three drivers combine: intense UV burns proteins, heat doubles oil and sweat, dry air pulls moisture out.

compounds.name: Heatwave Crisis
compounds.mechanism: Heatwave conditions — body and skin dehydrating; UV burns possible in minutes; barrier proteins denaturing.

compounds.name: Dry-Heat Desert Day
compounds.mechanism: Bone-dry desert air strips moisture while heat and UV pile on. Barrier is fighting on three fronts.

compounds.name: Beach Day UV
compounds.mechanism: Water and sand reflect 25–50% more UV. Heat plus humidity locks oil on the surface.
compounds.cities: Goa, Kerala coast, Chennai beach days

compounds.name: Hot-Humid Coastal Summer
compounds.mechanism: Heat doubles oil, humidity keeps sweat from evaporating. Pores stay occluded most of the day.

compounds.name: Monsoon Acne Trifecta
compounds.mechanism: Heat, humidity, and pollution combine. Sweat and oil cannot evaporate, particles settle into pores, and pollution drives inflammation.

compounds.name: Coastal Monsoon Standard
compounds.mechanism: Heavy humid air keeps sweat on skin and traps oil. Fungal risk in folds rises.

compounds.name: Tropical NE Saturated
compounds.mechanism: Air at saturation. Sweat won't evaporate. Pores and folds stay blocked.

compounds.name: Pre-Monsoon Humidity Surge
compounds.mechanism: Humidity surges before rains arrive. Heat is still high. Sweat-oil-UV trifecta peaks.

compounds.name: Delhi Winter Smog
compounds.mechanism: Inversion traps pollution; dry cold air cracks the barrier; pollution then seeps through. Worst combination for many concerns.

compounds.name: Post-Diwali AQI Spike
compounds.mechanism: Severe overnight AQI spike from firecrackers + inversion. Acute particulate-driven barrier and pigment insult.

compounds.name: Stubble-Burning Season
compounds.mechanism: Crop-residue smoke carries fine PM2.5 and PAH compounds. Direct AhR activation drives pigmentation and inflammation.

compounds.name: Industrial Belt Day
compounds.mechanism: Sustained industrial pollution oxidizes facial sebum into pore-clogging peroxides. Daily antioxidant defense matters.

compounds.name: Cold + Polluted Winter
compounds.mechanism: Cold cracks the barrier and dry air keeps it cracked. Pollution then walks through the open door.

compounds.name: North Indian Winter Dry
compounds.mechanism: Cold air holds little moisture; heated indoor air holds even less. Barrier under constant stress.

compounds.name: Hill Station Winter
compounds.mechanism: Cold + dry air + altitude UV. Snow reflects up to 80% UV onto unprotected faces.

compounds.name: Extreme Cold Mountain
compounds.mechanism: Sub-zero air holds near-zero moisture. UV intensified by altitude. Skin's lipid layer can physically crack.
compounds.cities: Leh, Srinagar peak winter; Ladakh year-round

compounds.name: High-Altitude UV
compounds.mechanism: Every 1000m altitude adds 10–12% UV intensity. Cool air masks the burn risk.

compounds.name: Snow-Reflected UV
compounds.mechanism: Fresh snow reflects up to 80% of UV — hitting under chin, nose, ears. Cold air masks the burn warning signals.

compounds.name: AC Transition Stress
compounds.mechanism: AC strips humidity to ~20%. Hours in AC + transitions outdoors create constant humidity-shock cycles for the barrier.

compounds.name: Indoor AC Office Hours
compounds.mechanism: Eight or more hours of AC-conditioned air at 20–35% humidity steadily pulls water from skin. Chronic dehydration accumulates even though no single hour feels harsh.
compounds.cities: All metro office workers; IT corridors; long-haul flights

nuggets.text: Dark skin already does some sunscreen-like work — it filters about 93% of UVB and 83% of UVA — but you can still tan, burn and develop dark spots.
In a Mumbai or Chennai summer the UV Index can hit 11–13 — 'extreme'. Even at UV 8, skin reaches damage thresholds within minutes.
Sunscreen plus an antioxidant serum layered together is about 4× more protective against UV damage than sunscreen alone.
Tinted mineral sunscreens lifted melasma improvement from 60% to 75% in 12 weeks — they block visible light that regular sunscreens miss.
Sweat strips up to ~40% of your sunscreen's SPF — which is why reapplying every two hours outdoors matters.
Skin's natural moisturiser only forms properly when surface humidity sits around 80–95% — too dry and production stalls.
Step from a humid room into dry air and your skin's water-loss rate can spike 6-fold; it takes about a week to settle.
In polluted megacities, skin's own protective oils — its first-line antioxidants — drop by roughly half.
One light dose of sun cuts your skin's stored antioxidants by about half; topping up from food and a serum both help.
A daily serving of tomato-rich food for 10 weeks measurably reduces UV redness — about 40% lower.
In eczema-prone skin, barrier lipids are down ~50% even in areas that look normal.
About 88% of Indians are vitamin-D deficient — the same melanin that protects from UV also slows vitamin-D making.
Live in a high-pollution city for a few months and skin literally makes less of its own moisturiser protein.
Every extra 10 units of PM2.5 raises facial pigment-spot scores by ~9% and wrinkle scores by ~3%. Pollution is provably a skin-ager.
Step from a 22°C room into 32°C heat and your forehead measurably makes more oil within an hour — 'hot day = oily skin' is real.
Most people apply about half the sunscreen the SPF claim assumes — and protection drops sharply at that amount. The two-finger rule helps.
Tinted mineral sunscreens block 80–97% of visible/blue light — the wavelengths that worsen melasma in brown skin.
Two well-studied oral photoprotection supplements each lift UV tolerance by about 26% over three months.

nutrition.effect: Around 88% of Indians run low on vitamin D — the same melanin that shields from UV also slows the skin's own vitamin-D making.
nutrition.direction: Low status → weaker barrier & slower healing
nutrition.source: Sunscreens for Skin of Color; Nutrition & Skin

nutrition.effect: Omega-3 fats calm UV-triggered inflammation and support the skin barrier.
A vegetable-rich diet tops up the skin's own antioxidant pool; tomato-rich foods cut UV redness ~40% over 10 weeks.
nutrition.direction: Higher intake → better defence vs sun & pollution
nutrition.source: Nutrition & Skin; Skin Stress Response Pathways

nutrition.effect: Two-to-three glasses of milk a day and high-sugar diets track with more acne.
Vegetarian Indian diets high in phytate bind zinc; low zinc shows as slower healing and breakouts.
Sunscreen plus an antioxidant serum is about 4× more protective against UV than sunscreen alone.
Two well-studied oral options — a B-vitamin form and a fern-derived extract — each lift UV tolerance ~26% over 3 months.

lifestyle.effect: Skin's repair runs strongest overnight; poor or shift sleep visibly ages skin and slows healing.
lifestyle.source: Skin Stress Response Pathways; Sleep disorders in women (DOI 10.1055/a-2371-0763)

lifestyle.effect: High stress measurably slows barrier recovery and lowers the skin's own defences — more flares and breakouts.
Adds visible wrinkles (forehead, mouth, crow's feet) and dulls tone.
lifestyle.source: Impact of Smoking & Alcohol on Facial Aging

lifestyle.effect: Drives facial volume loss and raises facial-flushing / nasal-redness odds by ~60%.
Sweat salts and pro-itch signals irritate eczema-prone skin; a quick post-sweat rinse helps.
lifestyle.source: Immunology of the Skin; Atopic Dermatitis

lifestyle.effect: Hormone shifts (cycle, pregnancy, perimenopause) swing oil, pigment and sensitivity; melasma and acne often track them.
Long screens, eye-rubbing and short sleep are top modifiable drivers of under-eye darkness in Indian women.
lifestyle.direction: More screens / less sleep → darker under-eyes
